context:
Data: Eurostat HICP, euro area* = the 21 current members at every date, chain-linked bottom-up from six components. Last published month: Sep 2026. The forecast covers the next three months.
Selected component models (pre-committed rule: keep the simpler model unless a richer one is significantly better, Diebold-Mariano test, chosen on 2010-2019 origins): fuels: Weekly Oil Bulletin pump prices; electricity and gas: seasonal mean of monthly changes; processed food: AR(p) chosen by AIC; unprocessed food: seasonal mean of monthly changes; non-energy industrial goods: no change in y/y (last year's monthly changes repeated; round 4, D57); services: no change in y/y (last year's monthly changes repeated; round 4, D57).
Base effect = the part of the change in y/y that comes from the monthly change a year earlier dropping out; it is known in advance. Momentum = the part from new monthly price changes.
The bands are empirical quantiles of the model's own past out-of-sample errors, not model-implied.
The shock simulator moves price levels per country and component; second-round effects are an estimated distributed lag. Actuals are final Eurostat releases; flash estimates are used only in the first-release check.
Model history: rounds 2 and 3 (pre-registered; round 3 tried SARIMA, Elastic Net, gradient boosting and an ensemble) found nothing that beat the random walk at three months. Round 4 (pre-registered) forecast services and non-energy industrial goods as 'no change in y/y' (their monthly changes repeat last year's); it passed the Holm test narrowly and beat the earlier bottom-up model, so it is now the published model. Core inflation is a by-product of the goods and services forecasts, so it is now forecast essentially as a random walk. Not modelled: country forecasts (only the euro area* headline is forecast and selected), ECB policy decisions, anything after the three-month horizon.
Italy: its published total differs from the weighted sum of its components by up to about a tenth of a point; the cause is not identified.
